subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or reject the tool call?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the permanent behavior determines how a denied sandbox capability is surfaced to users and agents.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warnings channel while preserving the current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a host or non-PTY path intentionally.

options.title: Adopt Fork PR After Decision
options.body: Use the open fork PR only after maintainers choose the semantics and require current proof against main.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning through the existing exec warnings channel while preserving the current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across exec PTY support, exec host routing, and the docs surface involved in this behavior.
